sentences.text: 2. Heard Sri M.S. Astagi, learned counsel for the petitioners and Sri Jamadar Shahabuddin, learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent No.1 - State.
Respondent No.2 though served, has remained un- represented.
Perused the materials on record.

3. In view of the rival contentions urged by the learned counsel for both the parties, the point that would arise for my consideration is:
NC: 2025:KHC-K:5187 HC-KAR Whether the criminal proceedings initiated against the petitioners is liable to be quashed invoking inherent power under Section 528 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023?

My answer to the above point is in the 'Affirmative' for the following:
REASONS 4. Respondent No.2 being the husband of petitioner No.1 herein, filed the private complaint in PCR No.106/2022 alleging that petitioner No.1 being the wife is making false allegations against him.
The other accused being her parents and brothers are also supporting such false allegations.

Petitioner No.1 had filed first information against respondent No.2 for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 323, 504, 506 of IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961,
which is now pending in C.C.No.9381/2022, for hearing before charge.

It is stated that petitioner No.1 has filed a petition under Section 12 of the Domestic Violence Act, 2005 pending in NC:
2025:KHC-K:5187 HC-KAR Crl.Misc.No.453/2021.
Similarly, petitioner No.1 has also filed another Crl.Misc.No.67/2019 under Section 125 of Cr.P.C. claiming maintenance.
In all these proceedings it is stated that petitioner No.1 made the allegation that respondent No.2 had demanded and accepted dowry at the time of marriage and even thereafter.
Therefore, it is his contention that false allegations are made against him with an intention to cause injury to his reputation and it amounts to defamation.
5. Relationship between petitioner No.1 and respondent No.2 is not in dispute.
Petitioner No.1 filing the above proceedings is also not in dispute.
Admittedly, all these proceedings are still pending consideration by the Trial Court.
It is for petitioner No.1 to lead evidence and to substantiate her contention regarding demand and acceptance of dowry, etc.

But in the meantime respondent No.2 has filed the private complaint seeking institution of criminal case, which according to me is Vijalaxmi And Ors vs The State Of Karnataka And Anr on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117415157/
3 premature.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: If petitioner No.1 is successful in proving her NC: 2025:KHC-K:5187 HC-KAR allegations regarding demand and acceptance of the dowry by respondent No.2, he is not entitled for any relief.

On the contrary, if petitioner No.1 fails to prove her contentions against respondent No.2,
then definitely respondent No.2 can initiate necessary action against petitioner No.1.
But during pendency of these proceedings before the Trial Court, it is premature to file and maintain the criminal proceedings against the petitioners.
Therefore, I am of the opinion that initiation of criminal proceedings against the petitioners is in abuse of process of law.

Accordingly, I answer the above point in the affirmative and proceed to pass the following:
ORDER (i) The Criminal Petition is allowed.
(ii) Criminal proceedings initiated against the petitioners in PCR No.106/2022 pending in C.C.No.294/2024, on the file of learned Civil Judge and JMFC at Basavakalyan, for the offences punishable under Sections NC: 2025:KHC-K:5187 HC-KAR 499, 211 read with Section 500 of IPC, is hereby quashed.
